title: Smooth-proper datum
statement: Fix the global finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], with $k_0=\Fq$ and $k=\Fbar$ its fixed algebraic closure. A *smooth-proper datum* $\mathscr X=(X_0,d,X)$ consists of a $k_0$-scheme $X_0$ [def-weil-scheme-over-base] that is smooth, proper and geometrically connected [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses] (proper, hence of finite type, so that $X_0$ is a finite-type $k_0$-scheme in the sense of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] and [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses]), an integer $d\geq0$ such that $X_0$ is smooth of pure dimension $d$ [def-weil-geometric-hypotheses] (its structure morphism is smooth and every irreducible component of $X_0\times_{k_0}k$ has dimension $d$), and the geometric fiber $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ of $X_0$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], the base change [def-pc-base-change] of $X_0\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$ along $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$. When $X_0$ and $d$ are given, 'the resulting smooth-proper datum' is $(X_0,d,X_0\times_{k_0}k)$. Every object later defined from $\mathscr X$ (the cohomological family, the Frobenius characteristic factors, the canonical integral factors, the Betti numbers, the determinant constants, the Euler characteristic and the functional-equation sign) is a function of $\mathscr X$, even when that argument is suppressed.

split_report.summary: Checked the statement against the slopmaster2 LaTeX (def:smooth-proper-datum, lines 2868-2876): it matches ('smooth, proper, geometrically connected F_q-scheme X_0, an integer d >= 0, an identification of d with the pure dimension of X_0, and the geometric fiber X = X_0 x_{F_q} k'); the closing convention sentence, which the LaTeX definition does not contain, is the convention of lines 2910-2911 of the same file, now cited in source.place. The statement is otherwise unchanged except that each notion is now tagged with the node that defines it, and a parenthesis records that proper implies finite type, which the geometric-fiber notation of def-weil-finite-field-fiber and the predicates of def-weil-geometric-hypotheses require. The notions the definition is built from: the global finite-field datum and the geometric fiber Y_0 x_{k_0} k of a finite-type k_0-scheme (def-weil-finite-field-fiber, reviewed), a k_0-scheme (def-weil-scheme-over-base, Mathlib leaf), the four predicates smooth, proper, geometrically connected and smooth of pure dimension d (def-weil-geometric-hypotheses, being split by another worker; not duplicated), and the fibre product/base change (def-pc-base-change). The integer d >= 0 is elementary. No new node was needed. Mathlib: the earlier search found the four component predicates (IsProper, SmoothOfRelativeDimension, GeometricallyConnected, GeometricallyIntegral); a further search for the base-changed scheme or a bundled datum found nothing, so the node is not a leaf. Lean: no declaration on either branch; the target weil_conjectures (WeilConjectures/Statement.lean) carries the datum as hypotheses [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] [IsProper f] [GeometricallyIntegral f] on f : X -> Spec k, i.e. geometrically integral where this definition says geometrically connected, as already noted on thm-weil-final.
